newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil up, trader buys again.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil up, trader buys again.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices rose on Wednesday as sellers backed off following Tuesday's massive purchase by two local traders.
The traders were still seen keen to buy more cargoes on Wednesday but the offers were at least 50 cents per barrel more than Tuesday's traded level.
A Europrean major sold Wednesday a cargo to the local trader at $26.70 per barrel for May 5-9 lifting, well above the $26.20/$27.00 traded level on Tuesday.
The same trader was bidding at $27.10 for a April 24-28 cargo but no sellers emerged for this cargo.
On Tuesday, two traders bought 1.35 million barrels, bringing their total purchases since early March to more than 10 million barrels.
The latest price hike may have triggered a new round of arbitrage exports from the West, with two vessels said fixed to arrive in end May.
Sources said two 60,000-80,000-tonne tankers are expected to load cargoes from the Black Sea and Rotterdam.
Currently, the East-West spread for May is valued at more than $3.00 per barrel, leaving the arbitrage wide open, traders said.
Already, about 1.6 million tonnes are due to arrive in this region from mid-April to early May, traders said, with the bulk of these cargoes sold to the local traders.
The latest buying frenzy also caused swaps prices to rise sharply late in the afternoon as the physical sellers entered the May market to hedge their sales.
May swaps were last quoted at $25.60/$25.70 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $24.90/$25.05, brokers said.
Jet fuel prices rebounded in a technical correction as sellers pulled back their offers to higher levels.
A 100,000-barrel cargo was offered at $25.10 per barrel, compared to Tuesday's $24.75 traded level.
